key_insight: AeroZoo shows that explicitly encoding boundary conditions can sharply improve aerodynamic flow predictions, while generalization to unseen enclosures and boundary-condition layouts remains difficult.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark tests whether neural CFD surrogates can handle new shapes and flow domains rather than only variations within one design family.
method: Generate 3,815 time-mean unsteady RANS solutions with a transition model across seven geometry families, eight enclosures and Reynolds numbers from 10³ to 10⁸.
Specify each flow problem using boundary meshes grouped by condition type, prescribed values and fluid properties.
Evaluate two tasks with engineering metrics and 22 geometry-disjoint splits using the 2,816 samples with stable time means.
evidence_signal: On the random split, boundary-condition tokens reduced GeoTransolver’s median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of inlet speed in single-seed runs; ISLA reached 5.3% over four seeds.
watch_item: ISLA’s error rose 2.4–9.2× for held-out enclosures or boundary-condition layouts, so random-split accuracy does not establish robust deployment generalization.
paper_title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
